<r>Benedictio.</r> Benedictióne perpétua benedícat nos Pater ætérnus.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<h>Lectio 1</h>
De libro Tobíæ
<r>Tob 2:1-4</r>
<n>1</n> Post hæc vero, cum esset dies festus Dómini, et factum esset prándium bonum in domo Tobíæ,
<n>2</n> Dixit fílio suo: Vade et adduc áliquos de tribu nostra timéntes Deum, ut epuléntur nobíscum.
<n>3</n> Cumque abiísset, revérsus nuntiávit ei unum ex fíliis Israël iugulátum iacére in platéa. Statímque exsíliens de accúbitu suo relínquens prándium, ieiúnus pervénit ad corpus,
<n>4</n> Tollénsque illud portávit ad domum suam occúlte, ut, dum sol occubuísset, caute sepelíret eum.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Peto, Dómine, ut de vínculo impropérii huius absólvas me, aut certe désuper terram erípias me: ne reminiscáris delícta mea vel paréntum meórum, neque vindíctam sumas de peccátis meis:
* Quia éruis sustinéntes te, Dómine.
<r>℣.</r> Omnia enim iudícia tua iusta sunt, et omnes viæ tuæ misericórdia et véritas: et nunc, Dómine, meménto mei.
<r>℟.</r> Quia éruis sustinéntes te, Dómine.
b.b28715b237:
<r>℣.</r> Grant, Lord, a blessing.
<r>Benediction.</r> May the Eternal Father bless us with an eternal blessing.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<h>Reading 1</h>
Lesson from the book of Tobias
<r>Tob 2:1-4</r>
<n>1</n> But after this, when there was a festival of the Lord, and a good dinner was prepared in Tobias's house,
<n>2</n> He said to his son: Go, and bring some of our tribe that fear God, to feast with us.
<n>3</n> And when he had gone, returning he told him, that one of the children of Israel lay slain in the street. And he forthwith leaped up from his place at the table, and left his dinner, and came fasting to the body:
<n>4</n> And taking it up carried it privately to his house, that after the sun was down, he might bury him cautiously.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> I entreat thee, O Lord, that thou wouldest loose me from this reproach, or that thou wouldest take me away from the earth:
* Remember not mine offences nor the offences of my forefathers, neither take thou vengeance of my sins; for thou, O Lord, art a Redeemer unto all that hope in thee.
<r>℣.</r> For all thy judgements are just, and all thy ways are mercy and truth; and now, O Lord, remember me.
* Remember not mine offences nor the offences of my forefathers, neither take thou vengeance of my sins; for thou, O Lord, art a Redeemer unto all that hope in thee.

<h>Lectio 2</h>
<r>Tob 2:5-8</r>
<n>5</n> Cumque occultásset corpus, manducávit panem cum luctu et tremóre,
<n>6</n> Mémorans illum sermónem, quem dixit Dóminus per Amos prophétam: Dies festi vestri converténtur in lamentatiónem et luctum.
<n>7</n> Cum vero sol occubuísset, ábiit, et sepelívit eum.
<n>8</n> Arguébant autem eum omnes próximi eius dicéntes: Iam huius rei causa intérfici iussus es et vix effugísti mortis impérium; et íterum sépelis mórtuos?
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Omni témpore bénedic Deum, et pete ab eo ut vias tuas dírigat,
* Et in omni témpore consília tua in ipso permáneant.
<r>℣.</r> Inquíre ut fácias quæ plácita sunt illi in veritáte, et in tota virtúte tua.
<r>℟.</r> Et in omni témpore consília tua in ipso permáneant.

<r>℣.</r> Grant, Lord, a blessing.
<r>Benediction.</r> May the Son, the Sole-begotten, mercifully bless and keep us.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<h>Reading 2</h>
<r>Tob 2:5-8</r>
<n>5</n> Cumque occultásset corpus, manducávit panem cum luctu et tremóre,
<n>6</n> Mémorans illum sermónem, quem dixit Dóminus per Amos prophétam: Dies festi vestri converténtur in lamentatiónem et luctum.
<n>7</n> Cum vero sol occubuísset, ábiit, et sepelívit eum.
<n>8</n> Now all his neighbours blamed him, saying: Once already commandment was given for thee to be slain because of this matter, and thou didst scarce escape the sentence of death, and dost thou again bury the dead?
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> In all seasons bless God, and ask of Him to order thy goings;
* And in all seasons let thy counsels be steadfastly in Him.
<r>℣.</r> Seek faithfully and with all thy strength to do such things as please Him.
<r>℟.</r> And in all seasons let thy counsels be steadfastly in Him.

<h>Lectio 3</h>
<r>Tob 2:9-11</r>
<n>9</n> Sed Tobías plus timens Deum quam regem, rapiébat córpora occisórum et occultábat in domo sua et médiis nóctibus sepeliébat ea.
<n>10</n> Cóntigit autem ut quadam die fatigátus a sepultúra, véniens in domum suam iactásset se iuxta paríetem et obdormísset,
<n>11</n> Et ex nido hirúndinum dormiénti illi cálida stércora incíderent super óculos eius fierétque cæcus.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Tempus est ut revértar ad eum qui misit me; vos autem benedícite Deum,
* Et enarráte ómnia mirabília eius.
<r>℣.</r> Confitémini ei coram ómnibus vivéntibus, quia fecit vobíscum misericórdiam suam.
<r>℟.</r> Et enarráte ómnia mirabília eius.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> Et enarráte ómnia mirabília eius.
b.daf9ad2119:
<r>℣.</r> Grant, Lord, a blessing.
<r>Benediction.</r> May the grace of the Holy Spirit enlighten all our hearts and minds.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<h>Reading 3</h>
<r>Tob 2:9-11</r>
<n>9</n> But Tobias fearing God more than the king, carried off the bodies of them that were slain, and hid them in his house, and at midnight buried them.
<n>10</n> Now it happened one day, that being wearied with burying, he came to his house, and cast himself down by the wall and slept,
<n>11</n> And as he was sleeping, hot dung out of a swallow's nest fell upon his eyes, and he was made blind.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> It is time for me to return unto Him That sent me; but bless ye God,
* And tell of all His marvelous works.
<r>℣.</r> Confess Him before all living, for He hath had mercy upon you.
<r>℟.</r> And tell of all His marvelous works.
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
<r>℟.</r> And tell of all His marvelous works.
b.d9697731d3:
<h>Oratio</h>
<c>K</c>ýrie, eléison. Christe, eléison. Kýrie, eléison.
<n><k>Pater Noster</k> dicitur secreto usque ad <k>Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:</k></n>
<c>P</c>ater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
<r>℣.</r> Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
<r>℟.</r> Sed líbera nos a malo.

<r>℣.</r> Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
<r>℟.</r> Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>D</c>írigat corda nostra, quǽsumus, Dómine, tuæ miseratiónis operátio: quia tibi sine te placére non póssumus.
<h>P</h>er Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.23d616bde0:
<h>Prayer</h>
<c>L</c>ord have mercy upon us, Christ have mercy upon us, Lord have mercy upon us.
<n><k>Our Father</k> is said silently until <k>And lead us not into temptation:</k>.</n>
<c>O</c>ur Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.
<r>℣.</r> And lead us not into temptation:
<r>℟.</r> But deliver us from evil.

<r>℣.</r> O Lord, hear my prayer.
<r>℟.</r> And let my cry come unto thee.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>M</c>ercifully grant, O Lord, that thine effectual goodness may in all things direct our hearts, forasmuch as without thee we are not able to please thee.
<h>T</h>hrough Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

b.2895de977e:
<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>U</c>ndécimo Kaléndas Octóbris Luna vicésima. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>I</h>n Æthiópia natális sancti Matthǽi, Apóstoli et Evangelístæ; qui, in ea regióne prǽdicans, martýrium passus est. Huius Evangélium, Hebrǽo sermóne conscríptum, ipso Matthǽo revelánte, invéntum est, una cum córpore beáti Bárnabæ Apóstoli, témpore Zenónis Imperatóris.
<h>I</h>n terra Saar sancti Ionæ Prophétæ, qui sepúltus est in Geth.
<h>I</h>n Æthiópia sanctæ Iphigéniæ Vírginis, quæ, baptizáta a beáto Matthǽo Apóstolo et Deo dicáta, sancto fine quiévit.
<h>R</h>omæ sancti Pámphili Mártyris.
<h>E</h>ódem die, via Cláudia, vigésimo ab Urbe milliário, pássio sancti Alexándri Epíscopi, qui, sub Antoníno Imperatóre, pro Christi fide, víncula, fustes, equúleum, lámpades ardéntes, ungulárum laniatiónem, béstias ac fornácis superávit flammas, ac tandem, gládio cæsus, vitam adéptus est gloriósam. Eius corpus póstea beátus Dámasus Papa in Urbem tránstulit sexto Kaléndas Decémbris.
<h>I</h>n Cypro sancti Isácii, Epíscopi et Mártyris.
<h>I</h>n Phœnícia sancti Eusébii Mártyris, qui, cum ultro Præféctum adísset et se Christiánum esse denuntiásset, ab eo, multis torméntis afflíctus, cápite cæsus est.
<h>I</h>n Cypro sancti Melétii, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.9b8462155f:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>S</c>eptember 21st 2027, the 20th day of the Moon, were born into the better life:
<h>T</h>he holy Apostle and Evangelist Matthew, who suffered in Ethiopia, where he had preached the Gospel. A copy of his Gospel written in the Hebrew language was, by a revelation from himself, found in the time of the Emperor Zeno, along with the body of the blessed Apostle Barnabas.
<h>I</h>n the land of Shaar, the holy prophet Jonah, who is buried in Gath.
<h>I</h>n Ethiopia, the holy Virgin Iphigenia, who was baptized and consecrated to God by the blessed Apostle Matthew, and fell asleep in a holy death.
<h>A</h>t Rome, the holy martyr Pamphilus.
<h>L</h>ikewise at Rome, at the twentieth milestone from the city upon the Claudian Way, the holy Bishop and martyr Pope Alexander I. Under the Emperor Antonine, he, for Christ's faith's sake, overcame fettering, cudgelling, racking, burning with lamps, tearing with hooks, exposure to wild beasts, and the fire of a furnace, and being at last beheaded won the life of glory that fadeth not away. The blessed Pope Damasus afterwards brought his body into the city on the 26th day of November, upon the which day he commanded a feast to be kept in his honour.
<h>I</h>n Cyprus, the holy Bishop and martyr Isacius.
<h>I</h>n Phoenicia, the holy martyr Eusebius, who went openly to the Prefect and proclaimed himself a Christian, for the which cause he was put to many torments and then beheaded.
<h>I</h>n Cyprus, the holy Bishop and Confessor Meletius.
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.
